name.text: Interpret the text and use the information to calculate conditional probabilities

questiontext.text:
During an epidemic in a town, {@aa@}% of its inhabitants became sick. Of any {@100@} sick persons, {@cc@} will need to be admitted to an emergency ward. What is the probability that a randomly chosen person from this town will be admitted to an emergency ward? [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

Give answer correct to 2 decimal places

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

Let

\(A=\) the person is healthy

and

\(B=\) the person is admitted to an emergency ward

It is given

\(P(A^{C})={@ee@}\)

Hence,

\(P(A)={@dd_1@}\)

We want to find \(P(B)\). Now \(P(B|A)=0\), because a heathy person will not be admitted to an emergency ward. Also,

\(P(B|A^{C})=\frac{{@cc@}}{100}={@ta_1@}\)

Hence, by the total probability rule,

\( \begin{align} P(B) &=P(A)P(B|A)+P(A^C)P(B|A^C) \\ &={@dd_1@}\cdot 0+{@ee@}\cdot {@ff_1@} \\ &= {@(dd_1*0)+(ee*ff_1)@}\\ &={@ta@} \end{align} \)

prtcorrect.text: Correct answer, well done.

prtpartiallycorrect.text: Your answer is partially correct.

prtincorrect.text: Incorrect answer.

truefeedback.text: You seem to have interchanged the P(A) with P(A^C)
